title: Regulatory Readiness: Authorisation and Supervisory Engagement
summary: A ten-module programme taking firms from licence application through to established supervision, showing how authorities assess applications and supervise new firms.
intro: This training programme equips firms applying for a licence or expanding their permissions to prepare a credible application, meet conditions after authorisation and engage with supervision, taught by former supervisors who have assessed applications.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give applicant and growing firms an insider's understanding of how authorities assess applications and supervise newly authorised firms. Participants leave able to prepare an application that answers the regulator's questions before they are asked, and to build the governance, resources and relationships that carry the firm through its first supervisory cycle.
sections.What It Covers: The business plan and regulatory business model, governance and fit and proper people, policies and procedures, financial resources, outsourcing and substance, the application process and regulator questions, conditions and post-authorisation, supervisory visits and risk assessments, remediation programmes and change in control.
Intended Audience: Founders, executives and directors of firms applying for a licence or new permissions
Compliance, risk, legal and finance staff preparing applications or variations
Advisers and project managers supporting authorisation, expansion or acquisition projects
Learning Objectives: Explain how authorities assess applications and what makes an application credible
Design a regulatory business model, governance structure and financial resources plan that meet threshold conditions
Prepare policies, procedures, outsourcing arrangements and local substance that withstand scrutiny
Apply practical techniques to manage the application process and respond to regulator questions
Assess how supervisors risk-assess newly authorised firms and plan visits
Manage conditions, remediation programmes and change in control with confidence
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines an assessor's-eye view with case studies, mock interviews and practical checklists, and modules can be selected or tailored to the firm's business model.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some familiarity with financial services regulation or the firm's proposed business is helpful. No prior experience of an application is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision (2024)
IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)
IMF, Good Supervision: Lessons from the Field (Working Paper WP/23/181, 2023)

modules.title: The Business Plan and Regulatory Business Model
modules.summary: How to present a business plan that explains what the firm will do, for whom and how it will make money, in the terms an authority uses to judge viability and risk.
objectives: Explain what authorities look for in a business plan and financial projections
Map proposed activities to the correct permissions and regulatory obligations
Identify business model features that attract supervisory concern
syllabus: Activities, permissions and the regulatory perimeter
Target customers, distribution and revenue model
Financial projections, assumptions and sensitivity analysis
Business model red flags seen from the assessor's side

modules.title: Governance and Fit and Proper People
modules.summary: Designing a board, committee structure and senior management team that the authority will accept, and preparing individuals for fitness and propriety assessment and interviews.
objectives: Design governance arrangements proportionate to the firm's size and risk
Assess candidates against fitness, propriety and time commitment expectations
Prepare directors and key function holders for regulatory interviews
syllabus: Board composition, independence and committees
Key function holders and senior manager accountability regimes
Fitness, propriety, competence and time commitment
Preparing for and handling competence interviews

modules.title: Policies, Procedures and Control Frameworks
modules.summary: Building a policy and procedure set that is tailored to the firm, operational from day one and clearly linked to the risks in the business plan.
objectives: Identify the core policies and procedures an applicant must have in place
Design documents that are specific to the firm rather than generic templates
Link policies to controls, monitoring and management information
syllabus: The core policy suite: compliance, risk, financial crime and conduct
Avoiding off-the-shelf documents that authorities reject
Compliance monitoring plans and risk registers at launch
Evidencing that policies are owned and operational

modules.title: Financial Resources and Wind-Down Planning
modules.summary: Demonstrating that the firm will hold adequate capital and liquidity from launch, under stress and in an orderly wind-down.
objectives: Calculate regulatory capital and liquidity requirements for the proposed business
Assess additional resources needed for risks and stressed scenarios
Design a credible wind-down plan and supporting financial projections
syllabus: Initial capital and ongoing regulatory requirements
Internal capital and liquidity self-assessment for new firms
Stress scenarios and capital planning
Wind-down plans: triggers, costs and timelines

modules.title: Outsourcing, Group Reliance and Substance
modules.summary: Meeting authority expectations on outsourcing, intra-group arrangements and local substance, so that the firm is genuinely run and controlled from where it is licensed.
objectives: Explain authority expectations on substance, mind and management
Design outsourcing and intra-group arrangements that keep control in the firm
Assess the risks of letterbox structures and over-reliance on group
syllabus: Substance: people, decision-making and local presence
Outsourcing due diligence, contracts and oversight
Intra-group services, delegation and conflicts of interest
Letterbox risk and how assessors test real control

modules.title: The Application Process and Regulator Questions
modules.summary: Running the application as a managed project, from pre-application meetings to handling rounds of questions, timelines and the authority's decision.
objectives: Plan an application project with realistic timelines and ownership
Apply effective techniques for pre-application engagement and meetings
Respond to regulator questions clearly, consistently and on time
syllabus: Pre-application meetings and setting expectations
Completeness, consistency and quality of the submission
Answering questions: tone, evidence and avoiding new issues
Why applications stall, are withdrawn or are refused

modules.title: Conditions, Restrictions and the First Year
modules.summary: What happens after authorisation: meeting conditions and restrictions, delivering commitments made in the application and establishing the firm's supervisory relationship.
objectives: Explain the types of conditions and restrictions attached to a licence
Design a post-authorisation plan that delivers commitments made in the application
Establish regular, constructive engagement with the firm's supervisor
syllabus: Licence conditions, restrictions and requirements
Tracking commitments from the application
Early supervisory engagement and regulatory reporting
Scaling governance and controls as the firm grows

modules.title: Supervisory Visits and Risk Assessments
modules.summary: How supervisors risk-assess firms, plan visits and form judgements, seen from the supervisor's side, so the firm can prepare and present itself accurately.
objectives: Explain how authorities risk-assess and prioritise firms
Prepare the firm for visits, interviews and information requests
Assess the firm's own position as a supervisor would
syllabus: Risk-based supervision and firm risk ratings
Visit planning, document requests and interviews
What supervisors test and the red flags they look for
Mock supervisory visit exercise

modules.title: Findings and Remediation Programmes
modules.summary: Responding to supervisory findings and running remediation programmes that fix root causes, deliver on time and restore the authority's confidence.
objectives: Analyse supervisory findings and identify root causes
Design a remediation programme with clear ownership, milestones and evidence
Report progress to the board and the authority with candour
syllabus: Findings letters and risk mitigation programmes
Root cause analysis and programme design
Independent expert reviews, attestations and remediation
Closing actions with evidence the supervisor will accept

modules.title: Change in Control, Expansion and Capstone Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together around change in control, new permissions and cross-border expansion, with a workshop in which participants test their own readiness.
objectives: Explain the change in control process and the authority's assessment criteria
Plan variations of permission and cross-border expansion
Produce a regulatory readiness action plan for the firm
syllabus: Change in control notifications and acquirer assessment
Variations of permission and new business lines
Branches, passporting and third-country considerations
Workshop: the firm's regulatory readiness action plan

related.title: Engaging Effectively with Your Supervisor: How Firms Are Assessed
related.summary: A ten-module programme showing firms how supervisors assess business models, governance and risk, so they can see themselves as the supervisor does and engage with confidence.

related.title: Fit and Proper for Firms: Appointing and Assessing Key Function Holders
related.summary: A nine-module programme showing firms how to appoint and assess key function holders, prepare applications and interviews, and manage fitness and certification on an ongoing basis.

related.title: Governance Reviews and Supervisory Interviews: Preparing Your Board and Management
related.summary: A one-day workshop on how supervisors assess governance and interview directors and staff, and how licensees can evidence effective governance and prepare openly.

related.title: Recovery and Wind-Down Planning for Firms
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping firms build credible recovery and wind-down plans, from scenarios and triggers to client asset return, testing and supervisory review.

related.title: Regulatory Investigations and Enforcement: Responding as a Firm
related.summary: A ten-module programme showing firms how to prepare for, manage and respond to supervisory investigations and enforcement, from first information request to settlement.

related.title: Supervisory Findings and Remediation: From Risk Assessment to Closure
related.summary: A one-day workshop on how supervisors reach findings and how licensees can respond with remediation that fixes root causes and closes issues on evidence.
